memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: the kings of Jericho one, Ai (near Bethel) one, Jerusalem one, Hebron one, Jarmuth one, Lachish one, Eglon one, Gezer one, Debir one, Geder one, Hormah one, Arad one, Libnah one, Adullam one - Josh 12:9-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the roll call begins in earnest — king after king, city after city, each followed by that simple word: "one." Jericho, one. Ai, one. Jerusalem, one. It reads almost like a ledger, a careful tallying up of every victory God had granted. Thirty-one kings in all before the list ends.

We might wonder why God's Word would spend verses on what looks like a bookkeeper's entry. But there is beauty in the detail. Each "one" represents a real battle, a real fear overcome, a real promise kept. God did not deal in vague generalities. He gave specific victories in specific places, and He made sure each was recorded. Nothing was lost in the summary; every single one was counted.

That same carefulness runs right through Scripture. The God who numbered these kings is the God who numbers the hairs of your head (Matt 10:30), who keeps your tears in a bottle (Ps 56:8), who knows each of His sheep by name (John 10:3). Nothing about your life is too small for His attention. The battles you have fought, the ground you have gained by His grace — none of it is overlooked. He counts each one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God notices the small, specific details of your life?
- What "one" victory in your life might God want you to count and remember?
- How does God's carefulness with detail comfort you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that nothing in my life is too small for You. You count each battle and know me by name. Help me to trust Your care over every detail. Amen.
